llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is most consistent with a sudden large DGD increase on the shared aerial fibre span E7. Multiple independent line receivers simultaneously measured about +66 ps DGD, increased pre-FEC BER, and then OTU_LOF, while optical power, OSNR, amplifier telemetry, and laser bias remained unchanged; this strongly favors a polarization-dispersion fault rather than loss, amplification, laser, ROADM, or OTN-switch failure.

proposals.rationale: E7 is the shared aerial span, and a DGD rise directly explains the nearly identical +66 ps DGD jumps, BER deterioration, and simultaneous failures across many channels without power or OSNR changes. The main limitation is that receiver DGD measurements do not independently pinpoint which span in the section introduced the dispersion.

Another span in the same shared OMS could produce the same receiver-side DGD and BER pattern. It is less likely than E7 because E7 is aerial and therefore more exposed to mechanical and environmental stress.

DGD introduced on this shared span would also leave power and OSNR largely unchanged while disrupting all traversing channels. There is no specific evidence favoring E8 over the exposed aerial span E7.

Wind or mechanical stress on the aerial span could cause a polarization transient and correlated errors. However, SOP rate showed no change and the sustained OTU_LOF and 300 errored seconds are much more severe and persistent than the documented millisecond-scale behavior.

Physical disturbance of the aerial cable could coincide with the abrupt onset. It is disfavored because the expected brief power excursion was not observed, whereas the dominant measured change was DGD.

A filter penalty can degrade signal quality without changing channel power and S17 is common to many impacted services. The documented fault is channel-specific and does not plausibly explain nearly identical DGD changes across numerous independent line channels.
